\section[the eight endings]{Review — the eight endings}

\label{lesson:ES-C09-repaso-ocho}



\begin{quote}
The first one you ever learned? (\emph{-ción} $\to$ \emph{-tion}.) The last? (\emph{-ario} $\to$ \emph{-ary}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Sorted by \textbf{what they make}, which is more useful than the order you met them:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{makes a thing} & \textbf{} & \textbf{makes a person} \\
\midrule
\emph{-ción} $\to$ \textbf{-tion} &  & \emph{-ante} $\to$ \textbf{-ant} \\
\emph{-dad} $\to$ \textbf{-ty} &  & \emph{-ista} $\to$ \textbf{-ist} \\
\emph{-ncia} $\to$ \textbf{-nce} &  &  \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{makes a describing word} & \textbf{} & \textbf{makes either} \\
\midrule
\emph{-oso} $\to$ \textbf{-ous} &  & \emph{-ario} $\to$ \textbf{-ary} \\
\emph{-mente} $\to$ \textbf{-ly} &  &  \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

Eight endings. Not one of them had to be memorised as vocabulary, because each is the \textbf{same suffix} arriving in Spanish and English by different roads.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: what each one costs you}]
Two things worth holding, because they save you a decision every time:

\textbf{Gender is decided by the ending, not by you.} \emph{-ncia} is always feminine. \emph{-ista} and \emph{-ante} never change at all. \emph{-oso} and \emph{-ario} end in \emph{-o}, so they shift when they are adjectives.

\textbf{Reach differs enormously.} \emph{-mente} is unbounded — it attaches to adjectives you have not met yet. \emph{-ción} reaches about two thousand words. \emph{-ario} reaches far fewer. They are all worth having; they are not all worth the same.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} the eight endings, and what each one makes
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which ending has no upper limit? (\emph{\textbf{-mente}}.) Which reaches about two thousand words? (\emph{\textbf{-ción}}.) And what did you memorise to get them? (\textbf{Nothing.})
\end{tcolorbox}
